Your homepage on a slow phone connection, and 8 ways to make it faster

We copied your homepage exactly as it is today and loaded it the way a shopper on a weak 4G signal would. Then we tried 8 changes, one at a time, and measured each one. Nothing here changes what the page shows or sells. Press "Show the next fix" to see what each change does, then approve the ones you want your developer to ship.

Same phone, same slow connection, same scrolling. Left is your homepage today. Right is with all 8 fixes. A shopper starts scrolling down at 2.5 seconds on both sides, at the same pace. The clock runs at real speed.

What to watch: the first picture shows up at about the same time on both sides. Then look at what fills in as the shopper scrolls. Today the search box, the chat button and the menu scripts arrive around 16 seconds in, and sections below the top keep showing spinners for longer. With the fixes the page is ready to use in about 5 seconds. Recorded on a Pixel 5 profile over slow 4G, filmed by the browser itself, with the same scroll script on both sides. The numbers above the fixes, measured separately and without scrolling, are the record.

The top banner rotates on its own, so the two pictures can show different slides. That is the page working as usual, not a change.

The fixes, in the order to ship them

What we cannot fix from outside

After the page arrives, its code keeps the phone busy for about 2.4 seconds building the page. None of the 8 fixes change that. It needs your developers to rework the app itself, which is a bigger project. Worth doing after the 8 fixes above are live.

What happens next

"Let the agent do it" asks ecomOS to prepare the change on a copy of the site for you to review; nothing changes on the live site until you say so. "Send to developer" opens the exact instructions to copy and send. Fixes 1 and 2 go live together. Fix 3 waits for your marketing team's yes. The rest can ship any time.

How we measured: a Pixel 5 phone profile on a slow 4G connection, 3 loads per version, the middle result. "Fully loaded" is when everything on the page has arrived. "Banner shows" is when the big top image is on screen. Real visits will be slower than these numbers because they also include your server and network, but the savings carry over.

Instructions

Copy this and send it to your developer as it is. It says what to change, where, how to check it worked, and how to undo it.
